checks_performed: Read only the two authorized JSON source files; used no web or other source material.
Compared the exact universal target with the draft's claimed resolution and final writeup.
Reconstructed every reduction, extremal-path argument, minimal-counterexample normalization, ceiling implication, disjoint-set count, and tournament argument independently.
Checked that the rainbow results stated in the authorized source apply to the tail-colored graph with n vertices, n colors, and color-class size d.

Ran an integer-only checker which exhaustively tested 25 triangle-free oriented three-vertex states, 163 locally admissible configurations in the d=3,n=10 argument, and all 45 parameter pairs with 2<=n<=10 and 1<=d<n.

claims.claim: Tail-color reduction: if D has no antiparallel pair, form an undirected graph whose edge {v,w} has color v whenever v→w. Every rainbow cycle in this graph is a directed cycle of D of the same length.
claims.evidence: Absence of antiparallel arcs makes the undirected edge and its tail color unique. On a rainbow cycle of length l, the l distinct colors are endpoints of the cycle's l edges and hence are exactly its l vertices. Thus every cycle vertex tails exactly one incident edge. Every vertex consequently has one incoming and one outgoing cycle edge, forcing a consistently oriented directed cycle of length l.
claims.search_method: Direct combinatorial reconstruction of the induced orientation on an arbitrary rainbow cycle.

claims.evidence: Selecting one outgoing arc at every vertex and iterating produces a repeated vertex among n+1 successive vertices. Taking the segment between the first suitable repetition gives a simple directed cycle of length at most n=ceil(n/1).

An antiparallel pair gives a 2-cycle, which is within ceil(n/2). Otherwise, retain exactly two outgoing arcs at every vertex. The tail-colored graph has n colors, each of size two. Theorem 1 stated in the authorized source, instantiated with p=0, gives a rainbow cycle of length at most ceil(n/2), and claim 0 converts it to a directed cycle.
claims.search_method: Case split followed by exact instantiation of the authorized rainbow-cycle theorem.

claims.evidence: If there were no antiparallel pair, the number of arcs would be at most n(n-1)/2, whereas minimum outdegree d gives at least nd>=n^2/2 arcs, a contradiction. Hence a directed 2-cycle exists. Looplessness gives d<=n-1, so 1<n/d<=2 and ceil(n/d)=2.
claims.search_method: Exact arc count in an oriented graph.

claims.claim: Every such D has a directed cycle of length at most n-d+1.
claims.evidence: For a longest simple directed path v1→...→vm, every outneighbor of vm lies among v1,...,v(m-1). The largest index j of at least d distinct outneighbors satisfies j>=d. The arc vm→vj closes a directed cycle of length m-j+1<=n-d+1.

claims.claim: There is a universal C<=10^11 such that every D has directed girth at most Cn/d.
claims.evidence: In the oriented case, retaining d outgoing arcs per vertex produces n tail-color classes of size d. The authorized source states a universal rainbow-girth bound C0 n/d with C0<=10^11, and claim 0 converts its rainbow cycle to a directed cycle. For the antiparallel case one may replace C0 by max(C0,2), still at most 10^11; then the existing 2-cycle satisfies 2<=Cn/d because n/d>1.
claims.search_method: Statement matching against the authorized source followed by the tail-color reduction.

claims.claim: For each fixed d there is a constant alpha_d>0 such that every D has directed girth at most n/d+alpha_d.
claims.evidence: The authorized source states the additive rainbow bound n/d+beta_d for a constant beta_d depending only on d. Applying it to the retained tail-color classes and using claim 0 proves the oriented case. Replacing beta_d by alpha_d=max(beta_d,1) also covers an antiparallel 2-cycle, since n/d>1.
claims.search_method: Statement matching against the authorized additive rainbow theorem and reduction analysis.

claims.claim: If a counterexample exists, one of minimum order can be taken oriented, strongly connected, and exactly d-outregular; moreover d>=3 and K=ceil(n/d)>=3.
claims.evidence: Choose a globally minimum-order counterexample. It has no antiparallel pair because K=ceil(n/d)>=2. Deleting excess outgoing arcs yields a d-outregular counterexample of the same order. A sink strongly connected component retains all d outgoing arcs; if proper, its order n'<n and its girth remains greater than K>=ceil(n'/d), contradicting minimality. Claims 1–3 exclude d<=2 and K=2.
claims.search_method: Minimal-order normalization, sink-component reduction, and previously established exact cases.

claims.claim: In a minimum-order counterexample, every outneighborhood S has minimum internal outdegree at most ceil(d/K)-1.
claims.evidence: For the normalized minimum counterexample from claim 7, every outneighborhood S has |S|=d<n. Let r be the minimum outdegree in D[S]. If r>=1, minimality supplies a cycle in D[S] of length at most ceil(d/r). Since the ambient girth exceeds K, ceil(d/r)>K, which implies r<d/K and hence, integrally, r<=ceil(d/K)-1. The bound is immediate when r=0.
claims.search_method: Proper-induced-subgraph minimality and exact ceiling arithmetic.

claims.claim: Every minimum-order counterexample satisfies n>=3d+2-ceil(d/K). In particular, when K=3 it satisfies 3d+2-ceil(d/3)<=n<=3d.
claims.evidence: After trimming, choose v with indegree at least d and let S=N+(v). Claim 8 gives u∈S with at least d-ceil(d/K)+1 outneighbors outside S. Such vertices lie neither at v nor in N-(v), since those alternatives create a directed 2- or 3-cycle. Thus {v}, S, N-(v), and those extra outneighbors are disjoint, yielding n>=1+d+d+d-ceil(d/K)+1. If K=3, ceil(n/d)=3 also gives n<=3d. Trimming preserves n,d,K, so the numerical conclusion applies to every minimum-order counterexample.
claims.search_method: Exact disjoint-set count after minimum-counterexample normalization.

claims.claim: If n<=2d+ceil((d+1)/2), then D has a directed cycle of length at most 3.
claims.evidence: Assume no directed cycle of length at most three and trim to outdegree d. Choose v with indegree at least d and set S=N+(v). The oriented graph D[S] has at most d(d-1)/2 arcs, so some u∈S has at most floor((d-1)/2) internal outneighbors and at least ceil((d+1)/2) external ones. These avoid v and N-(v), or else form a 2- or 3-cycle. Counting the disjoint sets gives n>=1+2d+ceil((d+1)/2), contradicting the hypothesis.
claims.search_method: Internal-degree averaging and exact disjoint-set count.

claims.claim: For d=3 and n<=9, D has a directed cycle of length at most 3.
claims.evidence: Under the contrary assumption, trim to outdegree three. For arbitrary v, the oriented three-vertex graph on N+(v) has no directed triangle and hence an internal sink u. Its three outneighbors avoid v, N+(v), and N-(v), yielding n>=7+d-(v). For n<=9 every indegree is therefore at most two, contradicting average indegree three. The checker exhaustively confirmed the sink property for all 25 triangle-free oriented three-vertex states and the integer contradiction for n=4,...,9.
claims.search_method: Deductive local-sink argument plus exact exhaustive enumeration of all relevant three-vertex states and integer bounds.

claims.claim: For d=3 and n=10, D has a directed cycle of length at most 4.
claims.evidence: Assuming girth at least five, the claim-11 count gives every indegree at most three; average indegree three makes the graph 3-in/3-out regular. For fixed v, partition the remaining vertices into S=N+(v), I=N-(v), and three nonneighbors R. No S→I arc exists. If every R vertex received from S, no R→I arc could exist without a 4-cycle, leaving each I vertex with at most two inneighbors. Hence some r0∈R receives no S arc. But S sends nine arcs into S∪R and has at most three internal arcs; the zero column forces exactly three internal arcs, making S a transitive tournament. Its sink must send to all three vertices of R, including r0, a contradiction. The checker enumerated 163 locally admissible configurations and found none with the globally forced zero R-column.
claims.search_method: Exact regularity and partition argument, independently checked by exhaustive bitmask enumeration.

claims.claim: The target holds for semicomplete digraphs.
claims.evidence: An antiparallel pair supplies a valid 2-cycle. Otherwise the semicomplete digraph is a tournament. Minimum outdegree at least one rules out a transitive tournament, and a shortest directed cycle in a tournament has length three by examining the chord between its first and third vertices. Since the minimum outdegree d is at most the average (n-1)/2, ceil(n/d)>=3.
claims.search_method: Tournament average-degree and shortest-cycle chord argument.

claims.claim: The target holds for every n<=10.
claims.evidence: Claims 1 and 2 cover d<=2; claim 3 covers 2d>=n; claims 11 and 12 cover the remaining d=3 cases. With d>=4, 2d<n, and n<=10, only (n,d)=(9,4) or (10,4) remain, and claim 10 supplies a 3-cycle, exactly within ceil(n/d)=3. The checker enumerated all 45 integer pairs 2<=n<=10 and 1<=d<n and verified both complete case coverage and that each supplied cycle bound is at most ceil(n/d).
claims.search_method: Exact exhaustive enumeration of all admissible integer parameter pairs, backed by the proved case lemmas.

claims.claim: For every 1<=d<n, the circulant digraph on Z_n with arcs i→i+s mod n for 1<=s<=d has directed girth exactly ceil(n/d).
claims.evidence: For any directed cycle of length l, its positive lifted increments lie in {1,...,d} and sum to a positive multiple of n. Hence ld>=n and l>=ceil(n/d). Conversely, with L=ceil(n/d), use L-1 increments equal to d and final increment n-(L-1)d∈{1,...,d}. All proper partial sums lie strictly between 0 and n, so the resulting closed walk is a simple directed L-cycle.
claims.search_method: Exact modular-increment lower bound and explicit simple-cycle construction.

target_evidence: The exact target requests either a proof of the universal Caccetta–Häggkvist bound or an explicit counterexample whose directed girth exceeds it. The draft supplies neither and explicitly says so; the authorized source likewise identifies the conjecture as open. The verified special cases, approximations, minimum-counterexample restrictions, and tightness construction are nevertheless material progress. Therefore the target is only partially resolved, and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
